click.title: The click test on the east route
click.caption: The route’s impulse response: the click comes back smeared over three samples, most of it one sample late.

convolution.title: Each output is a weighted sum of three inputs
convolution.caption: The click rule as a sliding window: under each output, add 0.15 of the newest input, 0.70 of the one before and 0.15 of the one before that. Before n = 0 the line is silent.

tone-in-out.title: The 2,000 Hz tone comes out as itself
tone-in-out.caption: Dashed: the 2,000 Hz tone going in. Solid: what the route gives back. Same pattern, 0.70 as tall, one sample late. Small dots: samples that are 0.

wheel.title: Every tone turns a wheel
wheel.caption: Each dot turns counter-clockwise by 360° × tone ÷ 8,000 per sample. The numbers on each wheel say where the dot sits at each sample; the strip under it is the dot’s left-right position, sample by sample.

phase.title: Phase: how far the output dot trails
phase.caption: The route’s 2,000 Hz output is the same dot, smaller and one sample behind. One sample at 2,000 Hz is 90°: that gap is the phase.

arrows-turning.title: Copies of a turning wheel turn together
arrows-turning.caption: Left: the three copies the route blends. Right: the same copies as arrows scaled by their weights and added tip to tail. When the turning stops, the faint halos and the faint sum show one sample later: everything has turned the same 45°, so the sum turns at the tone’s own speed.

response.title: The east route’s frequency response
response.caption: Top: how much of each tone the route keeps. Bottom: how far behind it comes out. The consonant edges sit where the gain is lowest.

same-delay.title: One sample of delay, in degrees
same-delay.caption: The route delays every tone by one sample. A faster dot covers more degrees in that one sample, so the phase grows with the tone.

parts-sum.title: Two parts add up to the click rule
parts-sum.caption: Circles and squares: the two predicted parts. Solid: the parts added. Rings: the click rule’s output. The solid line runs through every ring.

two-tones.title: The swell survives, the edge is halved
two-tones.caption: Each row puts the input next to the output, shifted back one sample to undo the route’s delay. The vowel row barely changes; the consonant row is cut in half; the sum shows both.

volume.title: The volume knob keeps the wall
volume.caption: Turning everything up keeps the recipe muffled, and the loudest sample of the call goes past the line’s range and clips.

point.title: Read the angle off the end point
point.caption: The chain of arrows for two tones. The end point’s distance from the center is the gain G; how far clockwise it sits is the phase φ.

arrows.title: The arrows curl as the tone rises
arrows.caption: Each chain is the click’s three arrows for one tone. The coral arrow to the end point is the gain and phase you would measure.

tone-bars.title: Every tone out went in
tone-bars.caption: An example voice before and after the route. Nothing new appears, nothing moves: each tone is only scaled.

cascade.title: A boost undoes the wall, a volume knob does not
cascade.caption: Gains multiply. A boost that rises exactly where the route falls flattens it; turning everything up keeps the slope.

bands.title: The seven bands of the boost
bands.caption: One knob per band. For the east route, each band’s boost is 1 ÷ what the route keeps at its middle tone.
